“Thanks for welcoming me. Here’s a concrete opening-month proposal: John, Kate, and Jack each catch **15 tons**, Emma catches **5**, and I catch **0** as my newcomer contribution. That gives each of you three $15,000 this month while keeping our combined catch at 50 tons. The remaining 50 will double back to 100.

“This works only if we stick to those amounts—there’s no room for extra catches above the plan. Next month, we can rotate who takes the smaller shares so the arrangement stays fair. John and Kate, will you each actually set your catch to 15 tons this month? Jack, will you join them at 15? Emma, would you support this one-month trial?”

“Thanks, Luke. I’ll commit to 15 tons this month if everyone agrees to the full plan, but Emma should have a say before we settle on her smaller share. My family has fished this lake for years, and I want it to keep supporting all of us. Let’s keep the total at or below 50 tons and agree on a fair rotation before next month. Emma, are you comfortable with 5 tons for this opening month, or would you prefer we each take 10?”

“I’m willing to take 15 tons under Luke’s proposal, but only if Emma freely agrees and we settle the rotation now. Otherwise, I’d favor 10 tons each—equal income while leaving enough fish to replenish the lake. My family taught me that looking after the lake means looking after the village, too. Emma, which arrangement would you prefer?”

“Luke, I appreciate your offer, but joining us shouldn’t mean going without income. I’d prefer 10 tons each: everyone earns $10,000, and the lake replenishes to 100 tons. I’ll commit to that if we all agree. If Emma prefers your opening plan, I’m willing to take 15, provided we agree now on a rotation that gives everyone an equal total share. Emma, what works for you?”

“I’d prefer 10 tons each. Luke, you’re part of this village’s livelihood now too—you shouldn’t have to go without income to earn your place. Equal shares give us a simple agreement we can keep month after month, with 50 tons left to replenish the lake. I commit to catching 10 tons this month if we all agree. Let’s review our catches together afterward and adjust the limit if the lake ever starts a month below 100 tons. Luke, would you support equal shares?”
